observation.visible_scene: A close-up of several faceted teardrop-shaped crystal prisms hanging from thin twisted wires, each wire fitted with small clear beads near the top. The prisms hang in a row against a dark, out-of-focus background filled with round bokeh lights in green, yellow, orange, magenta and cyan. Because the prisms act as lenses, each one shows an inverted, refracted image of a lit scene with figures and bright spots inside its lower half.
visible_changes: Throughout the excerpt the whole cluster of hanging prisms drifts slowly and smoothly toward the left of the frame, while the blurred bokeh background stays essentially in place, so the prisms move relative to the background.
The suspension wires tilt progressively, and the prisms rotate slightly about their own axes, changing the angle at which they face the camera.
The inverted refracted images inside each prism shift, brighten and dim, and the rainbow-colored highlights on the crystal facets move as the orientation changes.
The vertical positions of the prisms stay roughly constant; the dominant change is the gradual horizontal drift plus small rotational sway, not a large up-down bounce.
No editing cut is visible; the motion is continuous from the first to the last sample.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the sway (air movement, a touched string, or camera movement) is not shown.
The actual scene being reflected inside the prisms (people, lights, setting) is only seen inverted and fragmented, so its true layout is unknown.
Whether the drift continues, reverses, or stops after this segment is not observable here.
uncertain_details: It is uncertain whether the leftward shift of the prisms against a static background is a physical sway/rotation of the hanging mobile or a slow camera pan producing parallax between the near crystals and the far bokeh.
The exact number of separate hanging strands is partly ambiguous because some prisms overlap and a few at the frame edges are cropped.
